scope: The three Table 2 samples G-0 (unfoamed), G-1 and G-2 (PAS foam:paste 1:1 and 2:1 by volume) with the shared design ratios, and the unheated-state values stated in the text. Values after 200–1000 °C exposure are given only as ranges or in figures and are not transcribed.
madeBy: AI transcription · mix-sheet skill v1 (source-text pilot)

materials.name: Fly ash
materials.detail: The low CaO content demonstrated that the fly ash was Class F fly ash based on ASTM C618.

materials.name: Sodium Hydroxide
materials.detail: Sodium hydroxide pellets (HmbG®, Sigma-Aldrich, Taufkirchen, Germany) and distilled water were mixed together to prepare a sodium hydroxide solution.

materials.name: Sodium Silicate
materials.detail: The main constituents of the sodium silicate solution (South Pacific Chemicals Industries Sdn. Bhd., Selangor, Malaysia) were 30.1% SiO2, 9.4% Na2O, and 60.5% H2O.

materials.name: PAS Foam
materials.detail: Polyoxyethylene alkyether sulphate (PAS) was utilised as a foaming agent to prepare geopolymer foam.

cures.text: The moulded mixture was placed at room temperature for 1 day, and it was further placed in an oven (60 °C) for another 1 day.

tests.method: total porosity by synchrotron X-ray tomographic microscopy
KD2 Pro transient line source (ASTM D5334)

findings.goal: Meets RILEM structural lightweight criteria (density, strength, conductivity)
findings.text: only G-2 (compressive strength of 21.5 MPa, density of 1.69 g/cm3 and thermal conductivity of 0.7 W/(m∙K)) met the RILEM requirements for the application.

notes.text: G-0 lost compressive strength (2.2–8.7%) between 400 °C and 1000 °C, while foamed geopolymer gained compressive strength (4.2–68.6%) at the same temperature exposure.
An exception occurred in G-1 at 800 °C due to strength loss (4.6%).

gaps: Table quotes are mechanical joins of the Table 2 row label and its cells; shared cells span all three samples in the source.
No absolute masses: fly ash:slag 80:20, 8 M NaOH, solid:liquid 3:1 and silicate:hydroxide 1.5:1 are ratios with unstated bases; activator mass, water and foam volume per batch are not given.
G-1 water absorption, apparent porosity, density and thermal conductivity, and all heated-state values, appear only as ranges or in Figures 3–9.
Cure recorded as heat (60 °C oven day); the first day was at room temperature and samples were stored 28 days at room temperature before heating, so test age is left null.
Every value awaits the second-reviewer check recorded in the batch audit before release.
